correctness.rationale: After standardization \(X_i=\sigma_iY_i\), the two gamma variables are iid and their sum/proportion factorization yields an independent Gamma-Beta pair. This makes the selected reciprocal \(E[(\sigma_JY_J)^{-1}]\) a pair of beta integrals. Their difference from a complete beta integral is the exact derivative of \([t(1-t)]^{n-1}\), giving the displayed closed form. Entropy-risk subtraction then leaves exactly one copy of this expectation minus \(\log(n/(n-1))\). Symmetry and monotonicity of \(r/(1+r)^2\), together with rigorous center and extreme signs, prove one and only one crossover.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly identifies the practical comparison as unresolved at the hierarchy level: simulations show non-comparability but do not say where each natural estimator is preferable. The finding gives the complete two-population decision map in one closed-form threshold for every \(n\ge2\). It explains the simulation phenomenon, supplies immediately usable estimator-selection guidance as a function of hazard heterogeneity, and is a natural exact completion of a comparison the source itself highlights.
